transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

It’s very likely the battery given its age and the intermittent nature of the fault, though it could also be the charger failing to top it up fully. Since you’ve already cleared filters and blockages, please check that the charging light comes on when docked and try a full charge cycle on normal mode. If it still cuts out after just 5-10 seconds even with a full charge, the battery is probably worn out and needs replacing. Make sure to let the unit cool down completely before testing again to rule out any thermal protection triggers.

Charger light comes on and the plug goes in fine. It's usually OK straight off the charger though, it's worse once the battery's partly used. Also worse on Max, where it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Is that enough to say it's the battery before I spend £60+?

That pattern strongly suggests a worn battery rather than a blockage or filter issue, especially since it fails sooner on Max mode and when partly used. At five years old, the cells have likely degraded significantly, which is why it holds a charge but cannot sustain power under load. While I can't be 100% certain without testing the voltage, this is the most common cause for these specific symptoms in older Dysons. You might try running it on Normal mode only to see if it lasts longer, but expect reduced performance. If it still cuts out quickly even on Normal after a full charge, replacing the battery is likely your best next step.
I'll try Normal mode, but I can't swap in another battery to test. It's not swollen or hot, if that matters. Is it worth the £60+ for a new battery then?

It is usually worth it for a five-year-old model, as a new battery will restore its full runtime and power on Max mode. Since you have already checked filters and blockages, and the charging light works fine, the issue is almost certainly the aged cells struggling to deliver current under load. The fact that it fails sooner when partly used or on higher settings suggests the battery can no longer sustain the required voltage. If it still cuts out after 5-10 seconds even on Normal mode after a full charge, then replacing the battery is the logical fix. Given the cost difference between repair and replacement, a new battery is likely your best option to get more life from the vacuum.
